title: NixOS Host Overview
description: Host health for NixOS machines scraped by node_exporter (+ optional systemd/textfile/smartctl exporters). Panels that need an optional scraper say so in their description and show No data without it.

panels.title: Hosts reporting
panels.description: Hosts with a live node_exporter.

panels.title: Scrape targets down
panels.description: Targets with up == 0. Sleeping laptops/desktops are expected to show here.

panels.title: Failed systemd units
panels.description: Needs node_exporter's systemd collector (services.nixosMetrics) — see dashboards/README.md.

panels.title: Reboot pending
panels.description: Needs the NixOS textfile metrics (services.nixosMetrics) — see dashboards/README.md. Hosts whose booted kernel/initrd/modules differ from the current system.

panels.title: Fullest filesystem
panels.description: Highest used-space percentage across all real filesystems.

panels.title: Hottest disk
panels.description: Highest drive temperature reported by smartctl_exporter.

panels.title: Current generation
panels.description: Needs the NixOS textfile metrics (services.nixosMetrics) — see dashboards/README.md. System profile generation number.

panels.title: Generation age
panels.description: Needs the NixOS textfile metrics (services.nixosMetrics) — see dashboards/README.md. Time since the newest generation was built. Grows when a host stops updating.

panels.title: Reboot pending
panels.description: Needs the NixOS textfile metrics (services.nixosMetrics) — see dashboards/README.md. 1 when the running kernel/initrd/modules differ from the installed system.

panels.title: NixOS release
panels.description: Needs the NixOS textfile metrics (services.nixosMetrics) — see dashboards/README.md.

panels.title: Failed units (empty when none)
panels.description: Needs node_exporter's systemd collector (services.nixosMetrics) — see dashboards/README.md.

panels.title: Systemd units by state
panels.description: Needs node_exporter's systemd collector (services.nixosMetrics) — see dashboards/README.md.

panels.title: CPU utilisation
panels.description: Share of non-idle CPU time, averaged across cores.

panels.title: Load per core
panels.description: 1-minute load average divided by core count. Sustained > 1 means CPU saturation.

panels.title: Pressure (PSI)
panels.description: Share of time tasks stalled waiting on a resource. More honest than utilisation.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: 1 - MemAvailable/MemTotal.

panels.title: OOM kills
panels.description: Processes killed by the kernel OOM killer.

panels.title: Filesystem used
panels.description: Per mountpoint, excluding tmpfs/overlay/etc.

panels.title: Filesystems projected to fill within 7 days
panels.description: Free space of filesystems whose 6h trend reaches zero within a week. Empty is good.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Read (+) and write (−) bytes/s per device.

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Fraction of time the device had IO in flight.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Receive (+) and transmit (−), excluding loopback and container/virtual interfaces.

panels.title: Errors & drops
panels.description: Packets/s with errors or dropped, receive + transmit.

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: hwmon sensors (CPU, board, NVMe, ...).

panels.title: Fans
panels.description: No data on machines without fan sensors.

panels.title: Battery
panels.description: No data on machines without a battery.

panels.title: Health
panels.description: Overall SMART self-assessment. Needs smartctl_exporter.

panels.title: NVMe wear
panels.description: percentage_used from the NVMe health log. NVMe only.

panels.title: NVMe spare capacity
panels.description: available_spare. NVMe only.

panels.title: New media errors
panels.description: NVMe media and data integrity errors added during the selected time range (the lifetime total is a cumulative counter, so only a change matters). NVMe only.

panels.title: SATA/SAS bad-sector changes
panels.description: New reallocated, pending, offline-uncorrectable and reported-uncorrectable sectors per interval, summed per disk. The raw counters are lifetime totals that never go back down, so this shows only when one changes: empty or flat at 0 is healthy, any bar is an event. SATA/SAS only. To see the totals, query smartctl_device_attribute{attribute_value_type="raw", attribute_name=~"Reallocated_Sector_Ct|Current_Pending_Sector|Offline_Uncorrectable|Reported_Uncorrect"}
